lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Welcome to JavaScript Demystified. Today we build Nova Market, a complete online store, with React Router in framework mode.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: A real store? With products, a cart, and checkout?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Yes. Along the way you will learn routes, loaders, actions, fetchers, sessions, streaming, error boundaries, and middleware.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: That is a lot of ground. Where do we start?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: With one command.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Create the project with [create-react-router|create react router], install the packages, and start the dev server.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The app folder holds everything. The file [routes.ts|routes dot t s] lists your URLs. The file [root.tsx|root dot t s x] renders the page around every route.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: What goes in root?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The Layout function renders the [HTML|H T M L] and body tags. Inside the head go Links and Meta. Inside the body go your page, ScrollRestoration, and Scripts.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The default export is App, and it returns an Outlet. That is where the current route renders.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Why do we need Scripts?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: It loads the JavaScript that makes the page interactive. Without it, you get plain server rendered [HTML|H T M L].

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The last file is [react-router.config.ts|react router dot config dot t s]. That is where you choose how the app renders. We come back to it.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Routes are configured in [app/routes.ts|app routes dot t s]. Each entry has a URL pattern, and the file of a route module.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The home page is an index route. The catalog is a route called products.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: How do I build a page for a single product?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Use a dynamic segment. A colon, then a name: products, slash, colon slug.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Now nesting. Give the whole shop a layout route, with a header and a footer.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: A layout route adds no URL segment. Its child routes render inside its Outlet.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: So the header stays, and only the page changes?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Exactly. Nested routes are also how React Router loads data in parallel.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The prefix helper adds a path in front of several routes, without a parent file. We use it for the account area: orders, and settings.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: And when somebody types a URL that does not exist?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Add a splat route. A star at the end matches everything else, so it works as a not found page.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Can I skip the config and use file names instead?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Yes. The [fs-routes|fs routes] package reads a file naming convention, and you can even mix both.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Every file in your route config is a route module. Its default export is the component.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Around it, you can export a loader, an action, meta, links, headers, and an error boundary.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: React Router generates types for each route. Import Route from the [+types|plus types] folder that sits next to your file.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Do params get types too?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: They do. In the product route, [params.slug|params dot slug] is a string. [loaderData|Loader data] and [actionData|action data] are typed as well.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Before more code, learn the loop that React Router is built on.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: A request comes in. The loaders of the matching routes run, and their data goes to the components. The page renders.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: And when the user changes something?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: They submit a form. The action runs and does the write. Then the loaders run again, and the page updates with fresh data.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Read, write, read again. You never copy server data into state, and you never refresh it by hand.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: So what is state for?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The interface only. An open menu, a focused input, a selected tab. Server data lives in loaders.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Loaders and actions run on the server. [clientLoaders|Client loaders] and [clientActions|client actions] run in the browser. Your components run in both places.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Nova Market gets its products from a catalog [API|A P I]. In the loader, call fetch with the [API|A P I] [URL|U R L], and return the parsed [JSON|jay son].

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Why not fetch inside the component with [useEffect|use effect]?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: A loader starts before the page renders. There is no blank screen, no loading flag, and the request comes from your server, not the browser.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: That means no [CORS|cores] problems, and your [API|A P I] key never reaches the client.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Nested routes load in parallel. The layout loader and the page loader start at the same time.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: When one loader needs two calls, start both, then wait for them together with [Promise.all|Promise dot all].

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: What if the [API|A P I] fails?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Check [response.ok|response dot ok]. If it is false, throw data with the status, and the error boundary takes over.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: A loader can return strings, numbers, dates, maps, sets, and even promises. The component receives them typed, with no extra work.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: A child route can read the data of a parent with [useRouteLoaderData|use route loader data]. That is how the header shows the cart count.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Some data only exists in the browser. For that, use a [clientLoader|client loader]. We come to it later.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: A loader provides data to a route before it renders. Export an async function named loader, and return an object.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The component receives that object as the [loaderData|loader data] prop.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Where does the data come from?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: From anywhere. Put your database code in a file that ends in [.server|dot server]. Server files are never bundled for the browser, and neither is the loader.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: So I can query the database directly, without an [API|A P I]?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Directly.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: On the first visit, the loader runs on the server and the [HTML|H T M L] arrives with the products in it. On later navigations, React Router calls the loader for you with a fetch.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Now the product page. Read [params.slug|params dot slug], and look the product up.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: What if someone asks for a product that does not exist?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Throw data, with a [404|four oh four] status. The nearest error boundary renders it. We add one soon.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Search belongs in the [URL|U R L]. A form with method get and an input named q navigates to products, question mark, q equals.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: In the loader, read the request [URL|U R L], and get the q search parameter, then filter.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Why not keep the query in state?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: A [URL|U R L] can be shared, bookmarked, and it survives a refresh.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Use Link for ordinary links. It renders a real anchor, so it works before JavaScript loads.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Use NavLink for navigation menus. It knows when a link is active, or pending, and passes both to your class name, style, and children.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: What does pending mean?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The user clicked, and the loaders of the next page are still running.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: For a global indicator, read the navigation from [useNavigation|use navigation]. When its state is not idle, show a progress bar in the layout.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Inside loaders and actions, use redirect to send users somewhere else.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The [useNavigate|use navigate] hook exists too. Keep it for moments when the user is not clicking anything, like a timeout.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Actions handle writes. Export an async function named action from the route module.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Render a Form with method post. React Router calls the action of the matching route, with the [formData|form data] on the request.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Read it with [request.formData|request dot form data], and get the fields you need.

lines.speaker: mallory
lines.text: I will submit an empty email address.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: That is why we validate. If a field is wrong, return the errors with data, and a [400|four hundred] status.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The component receives them as [actionData|action data], so you can show each message next to its field.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Why the [400|four hundred] status?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Only successful responses revalidate your loaders. A failed validation does not need a reload.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: When the order is valid, create it, and return redirect to the confirmation page.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: For a pending state, use [navigation.state|navigation dot state], or check [navigation.formData|navigation dot form data] to disable the button.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: If you see question mark index in a [URL|U R L], that is how React Router targets an index route. It appears automatically.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The cart has to survive between requests. That is what sessions are for.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: [createCookieSessionStorage|Create cookie session storage] in a file called [sessions.server|sessions dot server]. Give it a cookie name, http only, same site lax, and a secret.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: In a loader or action, call [getSession|get session] with the cookie header of the request.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Read values with get, write them with set, and send the session back with [commitSession|commit session], inside a [Set-Cookie|set cookie] header.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: What if I forget to commit?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Then the change is lost. Every change needs a commit.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Flash gives you a value that is read once. It is perfect for messages like added to cart.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: To log out, call [destroySession|destroy session] and redirect.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: A Form navigates. Sometimes you want to save something, and stay right where you are.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: That is a fetcher. Call [useFetcher|use fetcher], and render [fetcher.Form|fetcher dot Form] with method post and an action pointing at the cart route.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: So the [URL|U R L] does not change?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Right, and there is no new history entry. If the [URL|U R L] should change, use Form. If not, use a fetcher.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: A fetcher has its own state. Check [fetcher.state|fetcher dot state], and show adding, while it is not idle.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: When the action finishes, every loader on the page revalidates, so the cart count updates by itself.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Now make it feel instant. [fetcher.formData|Fetcher dot form data] holds what the user just submitted.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Read the quantity from it, and render the next state before the server answers. That is an optimistic user interface.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: What if the item is out of stock?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Return the error from the action. It arrives as [fetcher.data|fetcher dot data], and the optimistic value simply goes away.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Fetchers also load data. Point a fetcher form with method get at a search route, and submit it while the user types.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: You can also call [fetcher.load|fetcher dot load] with any route [URL|U R L]. It runs that loader, and gives you the data, with no navigation at all.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The results appear in [fetcher.data|fetcher dot data]. That is your live search.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: And [useFetchers|use fetchers] reads every active fetcher, which is how the header can show a pending cart count.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: After every successful action, React Router runs the loaders of the page again. That is why your [UI|U I] is never out of date.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Even the expensive ones?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: You can opt out. Export [shouldRevalidate|should revalidate] from a route, and return false for requests that cannot change its data.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Always return the [defaultShouldRevalidate|default should revalidate] value for everything else.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: To skip a single request, pass [defaultShouldRevalidate={false}|default should revalidate false] to the form, the link, or fetcher submit.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Use the revalidator hook when you want a refresh without a submission, like polling stock levels.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Reviews come from a slow service. Do not make the whole page wait for them.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: In the loader, return the promise without awaiting it. The critical data is awaited, and the slow data is streamed.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: In the component, wrap the reviews in Suspense, with a fallback, and read the promise with Await.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Can I use the use hook from React instead?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Yes. Pass the promise to a small component, and call use on it.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The page renders right away. When the reviews arrive, they replace the fallback.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Pending promises are rejected after about five seconds. Export [streamTimeout|stream timeout] from the server entry to change that.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: When a loader, an action, or a component throws, the closest error boundary renders in place of the route.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Export [ErrorBoundary|error boundary] from the root. Use [isRouteErrorResponse|is route error response] to detect thrown responses with a status. Handle real errors, and unknown values, too.

lines.speaker: mallory
lines.text: I broke the reviews. Nobody will see a white page now.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Put a boundary in the product route as well. Only that part of the page shows the error, and the layout and header stay.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Boundaries are for surprises and for missing pages. Use [actionData|action data] for form validation.

lines.speaker: guard
lines.text: I protect the account area.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Middleware runs before your loaders and actions, from the parent route down to the child, and back up after the response.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Create a typed context with [createContext|create context]. Then export a middleware array from the account layout route.

lines.speaker: guard
lines.text: Nobody gets in without a session.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The middleware reads the session. If there is no user, it throws a redirect to login. Otherwise it stores the user in context.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Every child loader then reads that user from context.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Add a logging middleware in the root, and you can time every request.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Is there a client version?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Client middleware runs in the browser during navigations. It does not return a response.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Some data only exists in the browser, like recently viewed products in local storage.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Export a [clientLoader|client loader]. It runs only in the browser, on navigations.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: It can call the server loader too, and merge the results.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: To also run it on the first page load, set hydrate to true, and export a [HydrateFallback|hydrate fallback] to show while it runs.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: [clientAction|Client action] works the same way, for writes that never need the server.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: A route without a default export is a resource route. It serves data, not a page.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The invoice route returns a file download. A products route returns [JSON|jay son]. A webhook route handles posts in its action.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: To link to one, use a normal anchor, or Link with [reloadDocument|reload document]. Otherwise the router tries a client navigation.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: In React 19, render title and meta elements inside your route component. Each product page gets its own title and description.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The meta export still works, and the last matching route wins.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The links export adds stylesheets and preloads. The headers export sets cache control for public pages.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Handle attaches anything to a route, like a breadcrumb label, which you read with [useMatches|use matches].

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: In the config file, [ssr: true|ssr true] is the default, so every page is server rendered.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Set [ssr: false|ssr to false] and you get a single page app.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Or keep server rendering and add a prerender list. The about page and the policies are built once, at build time.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Forms work before JavaScript loads, because they are plain [HTML|H T M L] forms. That is progressive enhancement, and you get it by default.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: With React 19.3 or later, wrap the outlet in a ViewTransition component in your layout, and page changes animate.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: To test components that use router hooks, render them with [createRoutesStub|create routes stub].

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: To ship, run the build, and start it with [react-router-serve|react router serve], or use a template for your hosting platform.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: You now have a complete store.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Routes map [URLs|U R Ls] to modules. Loaders read data. Actions write it, and loaders refresh on their own.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Fetchers save without navigating. Sessions remember users. Streaming, error boundaries, and middleware make it fast, safe, and resilient.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Thank you, Byte. Now let me build one.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: See you next time.
